neet_phy_u16_t11_1.working: Coherent sources must have the same frequency and a constant (time-independent) phase difference.

neet_phy_u16_t11_2.working: Independent lamps are incoherent, so their intensities simply add: I + 4I = 5I.

neet_phy_u16_t11_4.working: YDSE uses division of wavefront (A-II). A thin oil film uses division of amplitude (B-I). Independent lamps are incoherent, so intensities add (C-III). A laser is highly coherent (D-IV).

neet_phy_u16_t11_5.working: A is true. B is true, since I_min = (√I1 − √I2)² = 0 for equal amplitudes. C is false, because a biprism divides the wavefront. D is true; it follows NCERT's statement that the phase changes about every 10^-10 s. E is false, because narrow, closely spaced slits are needed.
